source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3 ("Nominations for county and rural councils")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Read on the page image: the News-Letter's Ballycastle section lists each division with its nominee (no party labels printed; the recorded party is not from this page). The Northern Whig's list of the same day (p. 3), cited before, does not carry this council.

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. Fourteen members were returned. Glenariff had two nominations, but Joseph Lynn was returned unopposed after the withdrawal of Alexander Stewart; the other divisions were unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Citation corrected (w19-bna-fix, Nov 2026): the Northern Whig page cited before (20 September 1946, p. 3) has no Ballycastle list; the member is named in the Belfast News-Letter of the same day, p. 3 (page image), which prints no party labels, so Party_As_Printed is cleared (the recorded party is kept). Party (w19-fixes2, 19 Nov 2026): the recorded UUP had no source, since the Belfast News-Letter list of 20 September 1946, p. 3 prints no party labels. No party is recorded (unknown), as there is no consistent evidence: he has no earlier return in the division (F. Black, N., 1939, is another man) and his return after (Daniel M'Couaig, Rathlin, 1949) carries no label. Renamed from 'Rathlin Island' to Rathlin (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Ballycastle Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Rathlin; the rounds were filed as Rathlin (1924, 1927, 1949, 1955); Rathlin Island (1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1961). This round was filed as 'Rathlin Island', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (rathlin-island) answers with a redirect to this one.
